messages:

Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing — expected load and SLOs

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to run a 6-week pilot on our customer-facing summarization endpoint. Quick details: average prompt+response is ~150 tokens, 99th-percentile response size ~400 tokens. Expected daily volume starts at ~1.1M tokens/day and we expect peak traffic windows that could hit ~4,500 tokens/sec (short bursts, ~5–10 minutes).

SLO: p95 end-to-end latency <= 350ms. Production must be private/dedicated (data governance).

I've attached a basic workload profile (lumenbridge_workload_profile.xlsx). Can you confirm a recommended slab size (GPUs) and what p95 headroom we should commit to for the pilot? Also call out fallback options if we need to scale beyond the slab briefly.

Thanks,
Claire Morris
Head of Platform — LumenBridge
claire@lumenbridge.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot sizing — expected load and SLOs

Logan — I reviewed the workbook and sketched an initial slab. Notes and assumptions below. I left the workbook with an example tab for our math (attached copy to thread).

Assumptions (from Claire’s sheet + clarifying calls):
- Avg response tokens: 150
- Peak burst tokens/sec: 4,500 (sustained 5–10 min window)
- Target p95 latency: 350ms (end-to-end, includes network + model inference)
- Model: customer will start on a 7B-ish open model, we will serve a quantized variant (q4/q5 profile)
- Request shape: many short requests; batching opportunities limited during peak microbursts

Throughput modeling (high level):
- Baseline throughput (single dedicated A100-80GB equivalent node, well-tuned q4_0): ~6,500 tokens/sec measured under continuous batching on 512-token sequences. However, for short-sequence microbursts and conservative p95 we use an "operational throughput" of 1,800 tokens/sec per GPU to account for cold cache, KV fragmentation, and networking tail latency.
- For LumenBridge peak of 4,500 tokens/sec: 4,500 / 1,800 = 2.5 -> round up to 3 GPUs to cover peak under optimistic steady state.

Headroom and safety cushions:
- Microburst multiplier: 1.6x (to tolerate 5–10 minute bursts + holiday multipliers).
- Cold-start & rollout buffer: +1 GPU reserved for warmup / canary traffic.
- Operational recommendation: commit to a 6-GPU slab (3 active + 1 warm reserve + 2 burst buffer GPUs). This provides ~10,800 tokens/sec operational capacity and ~6.0–7.0x the typical daily baseline, giving runway for spikes and incremental growth.

Latency notes: with this slab we expect p95 inference time to be well below 300ms for steady-state requests. Tail events (cache-cold or large context) could still breach 350ms — we recommend conservative request shaping and a small A/B canary to validate p95 in the pilot.

Thermal / infra items:
- Rack power: plan for +10% power headroom (6x A100-class GPUs + hosts ~32–36kW peak).
- Cooling: confirm customer rack PDU and cooling capacity; otherwise we set a soft limit on burst concurrency.

Fallback strategies:
- Immediate: allow burst routing to Redwood hosted pool (higher-cost, no SLA change) for short spikes > slab capacity.
- Degraded SLO: if hosting pool unavailable, fallback to a smaller local model (3B) for non-critical traffic to keep control-plane availability.

I'll update the workbook with explicit tokens/sec->GPU math and a side-by-side cost delta for 3 vs 6 GPU commits. Priya — can you weigh in on quantization/profile tradeoffs (q4 vs q5) and expected throughput uplift?

Kimberly Park
Capacity Planning Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot sizing — expected load and SLOs

Thanks Kim — quick add from SRE/Solutions perspective. I ran microbenchmarks yesterday vs our q5_0 quantization profile on a 7B model (80GB-class host) and saw ~1.6x median throughput uplift over q4_0 for short sequences, with p95 improvement in steady-state. Important caveats:
- q5_0 increases memory pressure slightly (host needs ~10% more workspace)
- KV cache warmup still dominates first-minute tail; recommend pre-warm strategy (small traffic ramp for 10–15 minutes before open to customers)

Operational recommendation (refined):
- Start pilot on 6x A100-equivalent GPUs configured as: 4x active (q5_0) + 1x warm reserve + 1x burst buffer. With q5_0, estimated operational throughput: ~3,000 tokens/sec per active GPU (conservative p95 accounting). That yields ~12k tokens/sec steady operational cap and supports the 4.5k token/sec bursts with room to spare.
- Burst plan: allow transparent overflow to hosted pool (policy: only used when slab CPU/GPU saturation >85% for >30s).
- Canary: roll out 10% of production traffic for 48 hours, measure p95 and rerun the workload profile.
- Commitment sizing: recommend an initial 6-GPU reserved contract for the pilot, with an option to step up to 8 GPUs if pilot p95 exceeds 320ms during the canary.

Costs & tokens: with the expected token mix, pilot monthly committed tokens ~1.2B tokens (we'll map price tiers in the deal doc).

Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Expected operational capacity: ~12,000 tokens/sec (conservative p95 accounting).
- Pilot monthly commitment (tokens): ~1.2B tokens.
- SLA fit: p95 <= 350ms expected; target p95 <= 320ms after canary tuning.
- Fallbacks: transparent burst to Redwood hosted pool; degrade to smaller local model if overflow persists.
